Case Study

Async TCP Layer 4 Gateway

High-concurrency asynchronous Layer 4 TCP gateway/proxy in C using epoll, timerfd, and signalfd

C11 epoll timerfd signalfd IPv6 Rate Limiting Lock-free Atomics

Architecture Overview

Client → [Gateway:8080] → Backend Pool (127.0.0.1:9001, 127.0.0.1:9002, ...)
                    ↓
            epoll Event Loop
            ├── Listener (accept)
            ├── Client sockets (EPOLLIN/EPOLLOUT)
            ├── Backend sockets (async connect + EPOLLOUT handshake)
            ├── Health probes (timerfd → async connect)
            └── Signal handling (signalfd)

The gateway is a single-threaded, event-driven TCP proxy built on Linux epoll. It terminates client connections at the frontend port, maintains a pool of backend servers per route, and distributes connections using atomic round-robin across healthy backends.

Key Design Decisions

    <li><strong>Single-threaded epoll</strong> — Avoids lock contention; scales to thousands of connections on one core</li> <li><code>epoll_data.ptr</code> with typed tokens — O(1) dispatch without FD-to-context hash lookups</li> <li><strong>Async backend connect</strong> — Non-blocking <code>connect()</code> + <code>EPOLLOUT</code> for handshake verification</li> <li><strong><code>timerfd</code> for health checks</strong> — Kernel-driven 5s timer, no userspace sleep loops</li> <li><strong><code>signalfd</code> for signals</strong> — SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGUSR1 delivered as epoll events</li> <li><strong>Ring buffers with dynamic EPOLLOUT</strong> — Backpressure handling without busy-waiting

Connection State Machine

<code>CONN_STATE_CONNECTING  →  CONN_STATE_ESTABLISHED  →  CONN_STATE_CLOSING
       ↑                      ↓                         ↓
   async connect         bidirectional           cleanup +
   (EPOLLOUT)              proxy                  deferred free</code>

Each client-backend pair forms a bidirectional tunnel. The state machine ensures:

    <li>Proper async connect handshake via <code>getsockopt(SO_ERROR)</code> on <code>EPOLLOUT</code></li> <li>Flow control: only register <code>EPOLLOUT</code> when ring buffer has data</li> <li>Deferred cleanup: sockets closed after both directions finish

Epoll Token Architecture

Every registered file descriptor carries an EndpointToken:

<code>typedef enum {
    TOKEN_LISTENER,       // Accept new clients
    TOKEN_CLIENT,         // Client ↔ Gateway
    TOKEN_BACKEND,        // Gateway ↔ Backend
    TOKEN_TIMER,          // Idle timeout (timerfd)
    TOKEN_HEALTH_PROBE,   // Backend health check
    TOKEN_SIGNAL          // SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGUSR1 (signalfd)
} TokenRole;

typedef struct {
    TokenRole role;
    union {
        ConnectionContext* conn;
        BackendServer* backend;
        struct { int route_idx; } timer;
        struct { int route_idx; int backend_idx; } probe;
    };
} EndpointToken;</code>

This enables O(1) event dispatch — no hash table lookup from FD to context.

Async Backend Connection

  1. Call connect() — returns EINPROGRESS
  2. Register EPOLLOUT on the backend socket
  3. When EPOLLOUT fires: getsockopt(SO_ERROR) verifies handshake
  4. Success: transition to ESTABLISHED, enable EPOLLIN both directions
  5. Failure: router_mark_backend_down(), immediate retry next backend

This design means zero connection latency penalty — the gateway never blocks on backend connect.

Health Check & Auto-Recovery

  • timerfd fires every 5s → router_sweep_health_probes()
  • For each DOWN backend without active probe: async connect()
  • Probe completion → router_handle_probe_event() verifies SO_ERROR
  • Success: router_report_backend_success() → backend back in rotation

No external health check process needed — entirely in the event loop.

Rate Limiting (Token Bucket)

<code>// Global bucket
max_connections_per_sec = 1000  // tokens/sec

// Per-IP bucket
max_connections_per_ip_per_sec = 50  // tokens/sec</code>

Implemented with C11 _Atomic counters — lock-free, minimal overhead. Rejects connections with ECONNREFUSED before accepting.

Metrics & Observability

Send SIGUSR1 to dump metrics:

<code>kill -USR1 <gateway_pid></code>

Output includes:

  • Total/active/failed connections
  • Total bytes read/written
  • Backend failures, health probes initiated/succeeded
  • Per-route backend status (ALIVE/DOWN, active connections, failure count)

Performance Characteristics

Connection Handling

  • Max concurrent: 1024 (configurable to 65536)
  • Ring buffer: 8KB (configurable)
  • Max epoll events: 256 per wait
  • Idle timeout: 30s (CLOCK_MONOTONIC)

TCP Optimizations

  • TCP_NODELAY (disable Nagle)
  • SO_KEEPALIVE with custom timing
  • MSG_NOSIGNAL (no SIGPIPE)
  • IPv6 dual-stack (IPV6_V6ONLY=0)
